**Verse 19 (Bereishis 1:19):**

This is straightforward. The existing translation is accurate.

**Verse 20 (Bereishis 1:20):**
Hebrew: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים יִשְׁרְצ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם שֶׁ֖רֶץ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֑ה וְעוֹף֙ יְעוֹפֵ֣ף עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם:
Existing: "And God said, \"Let the waters swarm a swarming of living creatures, and let fowl fly over the earth, across the expanse of the heavens.\""

Looking at the Hebrew:


- יִשְׁרְצ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם שֶׁ֖רֶץ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֑ה - "let the waters swarm swarming of living creature"
- וְעוֹף֙ יְעוֹפֵ֣ף עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י רְקִ֥יעַ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם - "and fowl that flies over the earth upon the face of the expanse of the heavens"

The existing translation captures the sense well. The phrase "swarm a swarming" reflects the Hebrew construction where "שֶׁרֶץ" functions both as the noun (swarming) and the root verb. A refined version would read: "Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and let fowl fly over the earth upon the face of the expanse of the heavens."

Refined: "And Elokim said, 'Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and let fowl fly over the earth upon the face of the expanse of the heavens.'"

**Verse 21 (Bereishis 1:21):**
Hebrew: וַיִּבְרָ֣א אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־הַתַּנִּינִ֖ם הַגְּדֹלִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַ

ֽחַיָּ֣ה | הָֽרֹמֶ֡שֶׂת אֲשֶׁר֩ שָֽׁרְצ֨וּ הַמַּ֜יִם לְמִֽינֵהֶ֗ם וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ע֤וֹף כָּנָף֙ לְמִינֵ֔הוּ וַיַּ֥רְא אֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־טֽוֹב:

Elokim fashioned the great sea creatures alongside every living creature that moves—those that teemed in the waters according to their kinds—along with every winged creature according to its kind. Elokim assessed that this was good.

The verse describes the creation of marine life and birds, each categorized by kind, with divine approval of the work.

Verse 21 captures the moment when Elokim blesses these creatures, instructing them to be fruitful, multiply, fill the seas, and let birds increase on land. This blessing marks the culmination of the fifth day's creative work.

Verse 23 marks the transition to evening and morning, establishing the temporal framework for the fifth day as a complete unit of divine activity.

Verse 24 begins the sixth day, where Elokim commands the earth to bring forth living creatures according to their distinct categories—cattle, creeping things, and wild animals—each to reproduce after their own kind, and the command takes effect as stated.

The structure now flows more naturally as "Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: cattle, creeping things, and beasts of the earth, each according to its kind" followed by "and it was so."
